title: 第三章 冷眼讥嘲少年心第四章 月下独酌问苍天
content_zh:
疼。
像有无数根烧红的钢针，在骨头缝里搅动，在脑浆子里翻腾。每一次微弱的呼吸，都牵扯着胸腔里撕裂般的灼痛。喉咙里堵着浓重的铁锈味，咽不下去，也吐不出来。
楚夜是被活活疼醒的。
意识像沉在冰冷的泥沼里，挣扎着，一点一点往上浮。最先恢复的是听觉，耳边是压抑的、断断续续的啜泣声，像受伤的小兽，细弱又绝望。那是娘亲的声音。
然后是嗅觉。浓得化不开的劣质草药味，混合着屋子里常年不散的霉味和潮湿的土腥气，直往鼻子里钻。那是他家破瓦房的味道。
最后，才是沉重的眼皮。他用了吃奶的力气，才勉强掀开一条缝。
昏暗的光线刺得眼睛生疼。模糊的视线里，是熟悉的、糊着旧报纸的破屋顶，还有一张近在咫尺、写满了憔悴和恐惧的脸。柳氏的眼眶红肿得像桃子，脸上泪痕未干，嘴唇干裂起皮，正死死攥着楚夜一只冰凉的手。看到他眼皮动了，柳氏猛地一颤，泪水又涌了出来。
“夜儿！夜儿你醒了！老天爷啊，你可吓死娘了！”柳氏的声音嘶哑得厉害，带着劫后余生的哭腔，手忙脚乱地想去摸楚夜的额头，又怕碰疼了他，伸到一半僵在半空，只是不停地掉眼泪。
“娘…”楚夜想开口，嗓子眼却像被砂石堵住，只挤出一点破碎的气音。喉咙火烧火燎，全身的骨头都在**。他艰难地转动眼珠，视线扫过狭小的屋子。窗户被厚厚的木板从外面钉死了，只留下几条缝隙，透进几缕惨淡的天光。门口的方向，影影绰绰站着两个高大的黑影，像两尊门神，把唯一的出路堵得严严实实。是楚家的护院！楚雄果然说到做到，把他们母子彻底软禁了！
一股冰冷的绝望，混合着滔天的恨意，瞬间攫住了楚夜的心脏，比身上的疼痛更让他窒息。他闭上眼，脑海里不受控制地闪过昨晚那地狱般的景象：楚雄冰冷的宣判、护院们狞笑的嘴脸、呼啸砸下的棍棒…还有最后那一刻，从后背脊骨深处爆发的、足以撕裂他灵魂的恐怖力量，以及那片混沌虚空中睁开的、吞噬一切的巨眼…
“枷锁…囚笼…祭品…”
那几个带着万古寒意和滔天恨意的字眼，如同魔咒，再次在他混乱的脑海里轰然炸响！一股源自灵魂深处的冰冷战栗瞬间传遍全身！
“呃…”他痛苦地蜷缩了一下身体，后背那块骨头的位置，虽然不再有昨晚那种火山喷发般的灼热，却隐隐传来一种深沉的、持续的、仿佛被什么东西禁锢住的钝痛感，像是在无声地提醒着他什么。
“夜儿！你怎么了？哪里疼？告诉娘！”柳氏吓得魂飞魄散，看着儿子脸上瞬间褪尽血色，身体痛苦地痉挛，手足无措，只能更紧地攥住他的手，仿佛这样就能抓住他流逝的生命力。
“水…”楚夜艰难地吐出这个字，喉咙干渴得快要冒烟。
“水！对！水！”柳氏像是抓住了救命稻草，慌忙松开楚夜，跌跌撞撞地冲到墙角一个破水缸边，拿起一个豁了口的粗瓷碗，舀了半碗浑浊的凉水。她小心翼翼地端过来，扶着楚夜的头，一点点喂他喝下去。
冰凉的液体滑过灼痛的喉咙，带来一丝短暂的慰藉。楚夜贪婪地吞咽着，半碗水下肚，感觉像是烧干的炉膛里浇进了一捧雪，虽然杯水车薪，但总算找回了一点活气。意识也清晰了不少。
“娘…我没事…别怕…”他看着母亲憔悴惊恐的脸，心像被一只无形的手狠狠攥住，疼得他几乎喘不过气。他强撑着，用尽力气挤出一点安慰的话。昨晚爆发的真相，那恐怖的幻象，那烙印在灵魂里的字眼…这些都不能说。说了，只会让本就惊弓之鸟的母亲更加崩溃。
柳氏看着儿子苍白虚弱的脸，听着他故作轻松的安慰，眼泪更是止不住地往下掉。她颤抖着手，用一块还算干净的破布，轻轻擦拭楚夜嘴角干涸的血迹和额头渗出的冷汗。
“夜儿…昨晚…昨晚到底怎么了？他们…他们都说你…你用了妖法…”柳氏的声音抖得不成样子，充满了恐惧和后怕，“娘不信！娘打死也不信！可…可你怎么能…”

“没有妖法，娘。”楚夜打断她，声音虽然虚弱，却异常坚定，“是他们逼人太甚。兔子急了还咬人…我只是…力气大了点。”这话他自己说出来都觉得荒谬，但此刻只能如此搪塞。他必须稳住娘亲。
柳氏嘴唇哆嗦着，看着儿子那双深不见底、却异常清亮的眼睛，最终只是用力点了点头，把所有的恐惧和疑问都咽回了肚子里。她信儿子。只要儿子活着，说什么她都信。
“娘…你的药…”楚夜的目光落在柳氏蜡黄的脸上，心猛地一沉。娘亲的气色比昨天更差了，嘴唇发绀，呼吸也比平时急促。那救命的药，昨天被楚河他们一闹，肯定又断了！
柳氏眼神一黯，下意识地避开了楚夜的目光，勉强挤出一个比哭还难看的笑容：“娘…娘没事。老毛病了，扛一扛就过去了。你…你好好养伤，别操心娘…”说着，她又剧烈地咳嗽起来，瘦弱的肩膀抖得像风中的落叶，慌忙用手帕捂住嘴，好一阵才缓过来，手帕上赫然染着刺目的暗红！
“娘！”楚夜目眦欲裂，挣扎着想坐起来，却牵动了全身的伤处，疼得眼前发黑，又重重跌回硬邦邦的木板床上。
“别动！夜儿你别动！”柳氏吓得魂飞魄散，扑过来按住他，泪水涟涟，“娘真的没事！真的！就是…就是咳了点血丝…不打紧的…”
看着母亲强装镇定、眼中却藏不住绝望的样子，看着那手帕上刺目的血迹，再看看窗外那被木板钉死的缝隙和门口那两个如狼似虎的护院黑影…一股前所未有的、冰冷刺骨的寒意，混合着滔天的怒火和一种被逼到悬崖边的疯狂，在楚夜心底轰然炸开！
不行！不能再这样下去了！他死不要紧，可娘亲怎么办？等着活活咳死在这座被看守的活人坟里吗？
昨晚那股力量虽然恐怖，虽然差点要了他的命，但它真实存在！那是他唯一能抓住的、打破这绝境的稻草！哪怕那根稻草通向的是地狱，他也得去闯一闯！
“娘…”楚夜的声音异常沙哑，带着一种破釜沉舟的决绝，“你躺下歇着…别担心…药…我去想办法。”
“不行！夜儿你不能去！”柳氏死死抓住他的胳膊，指甲几乎要嵌进他的皮肉里，眼中充满了极致的恐惧，“外面有人守着！楚雄他不会放过你的！你…你哪里都去不了！”
“我有办法。”楚夜看着母亲的眼睛，声音低沉却带着一种不容置疑的力量，“你信我。躺下，歇着。等我回来。”他轻轻挣脱柳氏的手，强忍着全身撕裂般的剧痛，挣扎着从床上坐了起来。冷汗瞬间浸透了他单薄破烂的内衫。
他需要时间。需要一点点恢复体力，哪怕是一点点。更需要…一个机会。
柳氏看着儿子惨白却异常坚定的脸，看着他眼中那种近乎疯狂的光芒，嘴唇哆嗦着，终究没有再阻拦。她只是无力地瘫坐在冰冷的泥地上，捂着脸，压抑的哭声断断续续地从指缝里漏出来。绝望像冰冷的潮水，再次将她淹没。
楚夜靠在冰冷的土墙上，闭上眼，强迫自己忽略身体里每一寸都在叫嚣的疼痛，集中精神，尝试着去感应后背那块骨头。这一次，没有昨晚那种狂暴的力量，只有一种深沉的、如同被巨石压住的滞涩感和隐隐的钝痛。那块“废骨”像是耗尽了力气，陷入了死寂。
时间在压抑的啜泣和门外护院偶尔不耐烦的踱步声中，缓慢地流逝。每一分每一秒，都像钝刀子割肉般煎熬。
不知过了多久，也许是半个时辰，也许更久。楚夜感觉四肢恢复了一点微弱的力气，至少能勉强站起来了。他睁开眼，看向门口的方向。
机会，需要自己制造。
他深吸一口气，那带着霉味和药味的冰冷空气刺得肺管子生疼。然后，他用尽力气，朝着门口的方向，沙哑地喊了一声：“外面…有人吗？”
门口踱步的脚步声顿住了。片刻，一个粗鲁的声音不耐烦地响起：“喊什么喊？老实待着！家主有令，不准出来！”

“我…我娘…咳血了…”楚夜的声音刻意带上痛苦和虚弱，断断续续，“她…她的药…断了…再不喝药…怕是…”他故意没说下去，留下令人心悸的空白。
门外沉默了片刻。两个护院显然在犹豫。楚雄的命令是看守，不准进出，但里面要是真死了一个…虽然是病痨鬼，似乎也晦气？而且，一个病得快死的老婆子和一个昨晚发疯被打得半死的废物小子，能翻出什么浪花？
过了一会儿，那个粗鲁的声音才隔着门板响起，带着施舍般的傲慢：“等着！老子去问问！”
脚步声渐渐远去。
成了！楚夜眼中闪过一丝寒芒。他知道，这些护院狗眼看人低，绝不会亲自去跑腿，多半是随便打发个路过的下人去药铺。这就够了！他只需要一点点混乱，一点点转移注意力的时间！
content_en:
pain.
It was like there were countless red-hot steel needles stirring in the seams of the bones and tumbling in the brain. Every weak breath was accompanied by a tearing burning pain in the chest. The strong smell of rust was stuck in my throat, and I couldn't swallow it or spit it out.
Chu Ye woke up from the pain.
My consciousness is like sinking in a cold mire, struggling to float up bit by bit. The first thing to recover was hearing. There were suppressed and intermittent sobs in his ears, like a wounded animal, thin and desperate. That was my mother's voice.
Then there's the sense of smell. The overwhelmingly strong smell of low-quality herbs, mixed with the perennial musty smell and damp earthy smell in the house, penetrated straight into the nose. That was the smell of his dilapidated house.
Finally, there are the heavy eyelids. He used all his strength to barely open a crack.
The dim light hurt my eyes. In the blurry vision, there is a familiar broken roof covered with old newspapers, and a face that is close at hand, full of haggard and fear. Mrs. Liu's eyes were as red and swollen as peaches, her face was stained with tears, her lips were chapped and peeled, and she was holding Chu Ye's cold hand tightly. Seeing his eyelids moving, Ms. Liu trembled suddenly, and tears welled up again.
"Ye'er! Ye'er, you're awake! Oh my God, you scared me to death!" Liu's voice was hoarse, with a crying tone for the rest of her life. She hurriedly tried to touch Chu Ye's forehead, but was afraid of hurting him, so she froze in mid-air with her hand stretched out, and just kept shedding tears.
"Mother..." Chu Ye wanted to speak, but his throat seemed to be blocked by gravel, and he could only squeeze out a broken breath. His throat was on fire, and all the bones in his body were aching. He rolled his eyes with difficulty, scanning the small room. The windows were nailed shut from the outside by thick wooden boards, leaving only a few gaps, letting in a few rays of pale light. In the direction of the door, two tall black figures stood like two door gods, blocking the only way out. It’s the nursing home of the Chu family! True to his word, Chu Xiong put their mother and son under complete house arrest!
A cold despair, mixed with overwhelming hatred, instantly seized Chu Ye's heart, suffocating him more than the pain in his body. He closed his eyes, and the hellish scene from last night flashed uncontrollably in his mind: Chu Xiong's cold pronouncement, the grinning faces of the guards, the roaring sticks... And at the last moment, the terrifying power that exploded from the depths of his back and was enough to tear his soul apart, and the giant eyes that opened in the chaotic void and swallowed everything...
"Shackles...cage...sacrifice..."
Those words, filled with eternal chill and overwhelming hatred, were like a curse, exploding in his chaotic mind again! A cold shiver originating from the depths of the soul instantly spread throughout the body!
"Uh..." He curled up in pain. Although the bone in his back no longer had the volcanic eruption-like heat last night, there was still a deep, persistent dull pain that seemed to be trapped by something, as if it was silently reminding him of something.
"Ye'er! What's wrong with you? Where does it hurt? Tell mother!" Ms. Liu was so frightened that she lost all her blood. She watched her son's face drain out of color and his body convulsed in pain. She was helpless and could only hold his hand tighter, as if she could catch his passing life force.
"Water..." Chu Ye said the word with difficulty, his throat so dry that it was about to smoke.
"Water! Yes! Water!" Mrs. Liu seemed to have grasped a life-saving straw. She hurriedly let go of Chu Ye and stumbled to a broken water tank in the corner. She picked up a cracked rough porcelain bowl and scooped out half a bowl of turbid cold water. She carefully brought it over, held Chu Ye's head, and fed him to drink bit by bit.
The cold liquid slid down the burning throat, bringing a brief moment of comfort. Chu Ye swallowed greedily and drank half the bowl of water. It felt like a handful of snow had been poured into a dry furnace. Although it was a drop in the bucket, he finally regained some vitality. My consciousness has become much clearer.
"Mom...I'm fine...don't be afraid..." He looked at his mother's haggard and frightened face, and his heart felt as if it was being tightly grasped by an invisible hand. The pain was so painful that he could hardly breathe. He held on and tried his best to squeeze out some comforting words. The truth that broke out last night, the terrifying vision, the words imprinted on the soul... these cannot be said. Telling her would only make her already frightened mother even more devastated.
Mrs. Liu looked at her son's pale and weak face, and listened to his pretentious comfort, and her tears couldn't stop falling. With trembling hands, she used a relatively clean rag to gently wipe the dried blood at the corner of Chu Ye's mouth and the cold sweat on his forehead.
"Ye'er...last night...what happened last night? They...they all said that you...you used magic..." Liu's voice was trembling, full of fear and fear, "Mother doesn't believe it! I won't believe it even if I beat her to death! But...but how could you..."
"There is no magic, mother." Chu Ye interrupted her, his voice weak but extremely firm, "It's because they pushed people too hard. The rabbit bites people when it's anxious... I'm just... a little stronger." He felt ridiculous saying this himself, but at the moment he could only prevaricate like this. He must stabilize his mother.
Mrs. Liu's lips were trembling, looking at her son's bottomless but extremely clear eyes, she finally just nodded hard and swallowed all her fears and questions back into her stomach. She believed in her son. As long as her son is alive, she will believe anything he says.
"Mom...your medicine..." Chu Ye's eyes fell on Liu's sallow face, and his heart sank suddenly. My mother's complexion was worse than yesterday, her lips were cyanotic, and her breathing was faster than usual. That life-saving medicine must have been discontinued again due to Chu He's trouble yesterday!
Liu's eyes darkened, and she subconsciously avoided Chu Ye's gaze. She forced out a smile that was uglier than crying: "Mom...Mom is fine. It's an old problem. It'll be over with a little help. You...you take good care of yourself and don't worry about mother..." As she said that, she coughed violently again, her thin shoulders shaking like fallen leaves in the wind. She hurriedly covered her mouth with a handkerchief, and it took a while to recover. The handkerchief was stained with a dazzling dark red!
"Mom!" Chu Ye's eyes were splitting, and he struggled to sit up, but the injuries all over his body were affected. The pain made his eyes black, and he fell heavily back on the hard wooden bed.
"Don't move! Ye'er, don't move!" Ms. Liu was so frightened that she rushed over to hold him down, with tears streaming down her face, "Mom is really fine! Really! It's just... I just coughed up some blood... It doesn't matter..."
Seeing his mother pretending to be calm but unable to hide the look of despair in her eyes, looking at the dazzling blood stains on the handkerchief, looking at the gap nailed by wooden boards outside the window and the two wolf-like black shadows guarding the courtyard at the door... An unprecedented, biting chill, mixed with monstrous anger and a kind of madness that was driven to the edge of the cliff, exploded in Chu Ye's heart!
no! This can't go on like this! It doesn't matter if he dies, but what about my mother? Are you waiting to cough to death in this guarded living grave?
Although the power last night was terrifying and almost killed him, it was real! That was the only straw he could grasp to break this desperate situation! Even if that straw leads to hell, he still has to try!
"Mother..." Chu Ye's voice was unusually hoarse, with a desperate determination, "You lie down and rest...don't worry...medicine...I'll find a solution."
"No! Ye'er, you can't go!" Madam Liu grabbed his arm tightly, her nails almost digging into his flesh, her eyes filled with extreme fear, "There are people guarding outside! Chu Xiong will not let you go! You...you can't go anywhere!"
"I have a way." Chu Ye looked into his mother's eyes, his voice low but with an unquestionable power, "You believe me. Lie down and rest. Wait for me to come back." He gently broke away from Liu's hand, endured the severe pain that felt like tearing through his body, and struggled to sit up from the bed. Cold sweat instantly soaked through his thin and tattered underwear.
He needs time. Need a little bit of recuperation, even just a little bit. What is needed more... is a chance.
Ms. Liu looked at her son's pale but extremely determined face, the almost crazy light in his eyes, her lips trembled, and she finally did not stop him. She just slumped down weakly on the cold mud floor, covering her face, and her suppressed cries leaked intermittently from her fingers. Despair was like a cold tide, drowning her again.
Chu Ye leaned against the cold earth wall, closed his eyes, and forced himself to ignore the pain screaming in every inch of his body. He concentrated on trying to sense the bone in his back. This time, there was no violent force like last night, only a deep, sluggish feeling and a dull pain, as if pressed by a boulder. The "waste bone" seemed to have exhausted its strength and fell into deathly silence.
Time passed slowly amidst the suppressed sobs and the occasional impatient pacing of the nursing home outside the door. Every minute and every second was like a dull knife cutting flesh.
I don’t know how long it took, maybe half an hour, maybe more. Chu Ye felt that his limbs had regained a little strength, and he could at least stand up. He opened his eyes and looked in the direction of the door.
Opportunities need to be created by oneself.
He took a deep breath, and the cold air that smelled of musty and medicine stung his lungs. Then, with all his strength, he shouted hoarsely in the direction of the door: "Is there... anyone outside?"
The footsteps pacing at the door paused. After a moment, a rude voice sounded impatiently: "What are you shouting for? Just stay there! The master of the house has an order and you are not allowed to come out!"
"I...my mother...coughed up blood..." Chu Ye's voice deliberately sounded painful and weak, broken and broken, "She...her medicine...has stopped...if she doesn't take the medicine...I'm afraid..." He deliberately did not continue, leaving a heart-stopping blank.
There was silence outside the door for a moment. The two nursing homes were obviously hesitant. Chu Xiong's order was to guard and not allowed in or out, but if someone really died inside... Even though he was a sick and consumptive ghost, it seemed unlucky? Moreover, what kind of trouble can an old woman who is dying of illness and a good-for-nothing boy who went crazy last night and was beaten half to death make out?
After a while, the rude voice sounded through the door, with the arrogance of giving away: "Wait! I'll go ask!"
The footsteps gradually faded away.
Done! A cold light flashed in Chu Ye's eyes. He knew that these nursing dogs looked down upon people and would never run errands themselves. Most of them would just send a passing servant to the drug store. That's enough! All he needs is a little confusion, a little distraction!
